sections.body:

Its purpose is to support the yogic community and provide high-quality instructions. The organization sets the standards for yoga schools and yoga teachers. Nirvana Yoga School meets all the standards set by Yoga Alliance and is a registered yoga school. Yoga teachers can select the teacher training to become a registered yoga teacher.

200-hour yoga teacher training is the basic level of yoga training that provides RYT 200 certification. After that, 300 hours of training provides an RYT 300 certificate and follows a more intensive approach. The highest certification course is 500-hour yoga teacher training and you will get an RYT 500 certificate after completing the course. This intensive training combines both 200 and 300-hour yoga teacher training.

Anyone can become a registered yoga teacher for every form of yoga including Hatha, Vinyasa, Ashtanga, etc. You must enroll in a minimum of 200-hour yoga teacher training from a registered yoga school to become certified. sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.body:
How can I become a yoga teacher?

In order to become a yoga teacher one should complete, a minimum of 200 hours of yoga teacher training course (RYT-200) from a Yoga Alliance-certified school.

Why yoga teacher training in India?

When you attend the yoga teacher training in India, you will get an opportunity to immerse yourself in the rich spiritual and cultural traditions that have shaped the yoga practice for centuries. India has many great talents when we talk about yoga teachers. So with thousands of yoga schools, India should be one of your first options to pursue a yoga teacher training course

Is a yoga teacher a good career?

Of course, it is. Becoming a yoga teacher can be a fulfilling career choice for those passionate about yoga and helping others. With increasing awareness of fitness and the importance of yoga worldwide, teaching yoga is undoubtedly one of the best career options.

What qualifications do you need to join yoga teacher training in Rishikesh?

There is no such specific qualification required to attend this course, This course is open to everyone. Since this course will be held in English, one should be able to follow English lessons.

What is the most popular yoga Teacher training course?

The most popular course is 200 hour Yoga Teacher Training course. The 200-hour certification is globally accepted.

Can a beginner do yoga teacher training?

Yes, a beginner can do yoga teacher training. However, it is advised to have a minimum of 2-3 months of experience in yoga.

Which is the best yoga teacher training course for a beginner?

The best courses for a beginner are 200-hour or 500-hour yoga teacher training courses. 200 hour cover beginner to intermediate level topics and the 500 hour cover beginner to advanced level topics.

How can I start teaching yoga?

In order to start teaching yoga, you should first complete either 200 hours or 500 hours of Yoga TTC from any Yoga Alliance-certified school and then register yourself as a certified yoga teacher in the Yoga Alliance.

Can you teach yoga without certification?

No, since yoga requires a lot of practice and a precise understanding of human anatomy, philosophy, asanas, and other aspects of yoga, one will not be allowed to teach without certification.

What is the fee for yoga teacher training in India?

The average fee for yoga teacher training in India starts from $800 USD including the accommodation and food facilities.

What is the highest level of yoga teacher training?

The highest level of yoga teacher training is 500-RYT stands for 500 hours Registered Yoga Teacher. This certification will be provided to those who have completed the 500 hours of yoga teacher training.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.body:
Ayurveda believes in a holistic approach to well-being that takes into account the harmony of the body, mind, and soul. Herbal therapies, dietary modifications, yoga, meditation, and lifestyle adjustments are frequently used as treatments in Ayurveda.

Ayurveda is based on the three life forces, known as doshas in the human body. They are known as pitta dosha, kapha dosha, and vata dosha. Each individual inherits a different combination of the three doshas. However, one is often more dominant than the others. An imbalance in the doshas leads to illness and health problems. Promoting health and preventing illness is the primary objective of Ayurveda.

Ayurveda offers individualized advice based on a person's dosha (constitution type), acknowledging that every person is unique. This personalized care has the potential to improve wellness and health behaviors.

Yes, you can learn Ayurveda if you are a beginner. It can be learned by anyone irrespective of age and experience.

Yoga and Ayurveda are both products of the old Vedic tradition, which offers a lot of intellectual, scientific, and spiritual knowledge. The goal of Ayurveda is to achieve internal equilibrium through herbal remedies, food habits, and lifestyle change and the goal of yoga is to perform asana, pranayama, and meditation to create physical and mental equilibrium. Together they offer a comprehensive approach to well-being.

sections.title: Rooted in the Ancient Traditions of Yoga
sections.body:
Hatha, Vinyasa, Kundalini, and many more; we teach a variety of yoga practices, all inspired by how they were taught thousands of years ago. Each style offers something different and focuses on a unique aspect.

Our conventional yoga workshops are ideal for both beginners and professionals who wish to understand the fundamentals of yoga and build a solid foundation for their practice.

Hatha yoga is the most popular in this case. It is a gentle, slow-paced practice that focuses on breath control, flexibility, and relaxation. Our expert instructors walk you through each position and help you improve your alignment and posture.

If you're searching for a more dynamic and energetic practice, our Vinyasa yoga courses may be for you. This branch of yoga is purely flow-based, which connects breath and movement. You will progress through a sequence of poses that are synced with your breath in our Vinyasa courses, gaining strength, endurance, and focus.

Our Kundalini yoga courses are a beautiful way to learn the deeper layers of the practice. Kundalini yoga mainly centres around awakening the body's energies and creating inner peace and harmony. That is why our Kundalini sessions blend dance, breathwork, and meditation to help you connect with your true self and tap into your inner knowledge.

sections.title: Training the Future Yoga Teachers of the World
sections.body:
Teaching yoga is not a skill you acquire by watching it done well. It demands a deep understanding of alignment, breath mechanics, sequencing, anatomy, and the subtle art of reading a room full of students at different stages of their journey. That is exactly what we built at Nirvana Yoga School .

Recognized as the best yoga teacher training in Rishikesh , our programs are rooted in the classical traditions that the city has been the custodian of for centuries. From Hatha and Ashtanga to Kundalini and beyond, students move through a structured curriculum that is as demanding as it is rewarding. You get to cover asana practice, yoga philosophy, pranayama, and teaching methodology in real depth.

What sets our graduates apart is the live teaching experience. Students step onto the mat as teachers, receiving direct feedback from instructors who have spent years in the classroom and on the mat themselves. There are no shortcuts here. By the time you complete your certification, you will know how to hold a space, adapt to your students, and carry the lineage of this practice forward with confidence and integrity.

And with a Yoga Alliance certification, your skills will be recognized globally.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.body:
What is Kundalini Yoga style?

Kundalini Yoga style is a form of yoga that includes repetitive practice of mantras, hand movements (mudras), meditation, and breathing techniques along with the asanas. The focus here is to awaken the enormous spiritual energy present in the base of the spine and move it in an upward direction along the energy chakras for spiritual enlightenment.

Can beginners do Kundalini Yoga Teacher training?

Yes, beginners can do the Kundalini Yoga Teacher Training course.

Why is Kundalini yoga so powerful?

Kundalini Yoga is powerful due to its focus on awakening spiritual energy, its holistic approach consisting of physical, mental, and spiritual aspects, and its use of intense practices like dynamic postures, breath control, meditation, and chanting to activate and channel energy, leading to transformations in consciousness and self-awareness.

What are the advantages of the Kundalini Yoga teacher training?

Kundalini Yoga teacher training offers enhanced teaching skills in Kundalini & Hatha Yoga, fosters personal growth through self-awareness, and enables graduates to lead impactful classes and pursue fulfilling yoga teacher career opportunities.

Is Kundalini yoga dangerous? Kundalini yoga can be intense due to its potent practices aimed at awakening energy. When practiced without proper guidance, moderation, and self-awareness, there is a probability of physical, emotional, or spiritual challenges. It's important to approach Kundalini yoga with caution, under the supervision of experienced instructors, to eliminate potential risks

How can one become a Kundalini Yoga Instructor?

One can become a Kundalini Yoga Instructor by completing a minimum of 200 hours of Kundalini Yoga Teacher training course certified by Yoga Alliance.

Do you offer The internationally certified Kundalini Yoga Teacher Training?

Yes, the Kundalini YTT courses that we offer are recognized by the Yoga Alliance and are internationally certified.

Can I Teach Kundalini Yoga Without Any Certification?

No, Since Kundalini yoga requires a lot of practice and theoretical knowledge, you must have at least RYT 200 certification in Kundalini yoga to teach Kundalini Yoga globally.

sections.title: Curriculum for Kirtan, Vocal & Instrumental Music Training

subsections.title: Chapter 1: Harmonium, Vocal Activation & Kirtan Training
subsections.body:
This chapter is designed to help students develop a strong foundation in harmonium playing, vocal expression, and kirtan participation. It brings together melody, voice, and rhythm in a simple and structured way, allowing participants to gradually build confidence in both individual and group settings.

Students are guided step by step—from understanding the basics of sound and notes to playing simple melodies, singing devotional songs, and coordinating both together. By the end of the course, participants experience a natural progression from learning to active musical expression.

What You Will Learn

Harmonium Fundamentals (drop-down) Students are introduced to the structure and functioning of the harmonium, including proper sitting posture, hand positioning, and bellows control. Emphasis is placed on producing a steady and balanced sound, which forms the foundation of all further learning.

Understanding Swaras (Notes)   (drop-down) The course begins with the basic musical scale (Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Dha Ni Sa), helping students recognize notes, develop pitch awareness, and build familiarity with the keyboard layout.

Scale Practice & Finger Coordination   (drop down) Through guided exercises and simple patterns (alankars), students improve finger movement, accuracy, and confidence while playing.

Introduction to Chords & Harmony (drop-down) Basic chord structures are taught in an accessible way, allowing students to understand how harmony supports melody in devotional music.

Vocal Activation & Breath Awareness (drop down) Students learn foundational voice techniques, including breath control, pitch stability, and vocal warm-ups. This helps in developing a natural, relaxed, and sustainable voice.

Mantra Chanting & Pronunciation (drop down) Special attention is given to the correct pronunciation of Sanskrit sounds, along with breath-aligned chanting practices that support clarity and rhythm.

Bhajan & Kirtan Practice (drop down) Participants learn simple devotional songs and understand how kirtan works as a group practice. This includes call-and-response singing, maintaining rhythm, and engaging with others musically.

Coordination of Voice & Instrument   (drop-down) A key focus of the course is helping students sing while playing harmonium, developing coordination and confidence.

Introduction to Raga & Musical Expression (drop-down) Students are gently introduced to the concept of raga and how it adds emotional depth and character to music.

Rhythm Awareness (drop-down) Basic understanding of rhythm (taal) is developed through counting, clapping, and internal timing, enabling students to stay steady while playing and singing.

Learning Outcome

By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
items: Coordinate the voice and the instrument together
Participate in and lead simple kirtan sessions

subsections.title: Chapter 2: Mridangam (Drum) & Rhythm for Kirtan
subsections.body:
This chapter focuses on developing a practical understanding of rhythm through the traditional instrument mridangam (drum). It is designed in a way that makes rhythm accessible even to complete beginners, while still offering depth for those with prior experience.

Students learn how rhythm functions within devotional music and how to support singing and harmonium through steady and expressive playing. The course emphasizes hands-on practice, coordination, and group interaction.

What You Will Learn

Introduction to Mridangam (Drum) (drop-down) Students are guided through the basic structure of the instrument, correct sitting posture, and hand positioning. Attention is given to producing clear and balanced sounds.

Basic Strokes & Sound Techniques (drop-down) Foundational strokes for both hands are taught step by step, helping students develop control and consistency.

Understanding Rhythm (Taal) (drop-down) Participants are introduced to the concept of rhythmic cycles and how beats are organized in devotional music. 

Common Rhythmic Patterns (drop-down) Simple and widely used patterns such as Dadra and Keharwa are practiced, allowing students to quickly begin playing along with songs.

Tempo & Timing Control (drop-down) Students learn how to maintain a steady tempo and adjust speed based on the flow of music.

Kirtan Accompaniment (drop-down) Students learn how to support kirtan using simple and steady rhythmic patterns. The focus is on maintaining flow, listening to the melody, and playing in a way that complements the overall group sound.

Coordination with Singing & Harmonium (drop-down) Participants practice playing alongside voice and harmonium, developing the ability to listen, adapt, and stay in sync.

Dynamic Playing   (drop-down)

Understanding how to vary intensity and energy during a session, from soft meditative rhythms to more energetic patterns.

Group Rhythm Practice (drop-down) Students experience playing in a group setting, which builds confidence and musical awareness.

Learning Outcome

By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
items: Play basic Mridangam (Drum) rhythms with confidence
Maintain a steady tempo and coordination

Being mindful involves being aware of one's environment and inner states. By teaching people to observe their thoughts, feelings, and other in-the-moment sensations without judging or reacting.

There are different techniques of mindfulness practices, such as walking meditation, eating meditation, mindful breathing, and others. One may try out different techniques in their day-to-day life to sustain their awareness of daily life.

Yoga cannot exist without awareness and mindfulness. The goal of both yoga and mindfulness is to still the mind in order to develop a closer relationship with the self. Both of these direct us to become aware of breathing, by paying attention to our body's feelings and learning to accept reality as it is at any given time.

The practice of mindfulness requires one to keep attention or awareness of the present moment without judgment. Mindfulness practices consist of formal meditations to sustain awareness in daily life.

One can start their mindfulness journey by understanding the concept and the techniques of mindfulness practices. Thereafter after trying the different practices, one can start to incorporate the formal practices in their real life.

Sitting for extended period of time which is common among office workers, may lead to musculoskeletal issues. These issues can be reduced with desk yoga.

One can perform simple stretches sitting on the chair or standing using the table and wall. Individuals can also incorporate breaks to practice mindfulness to rejuvenate themselves from stress.

Office yoga is safe and easy to perform and can be performed by any individual of all ages. Office yoga provides support for the postures with the help of a chair, table, and wall.

By performing stretches from time to time and being mindful of the sitting posture one may improve their posture. The right posture is to prevent your head from tilting and keeping your computer at eye level. Keep your back flat on the chair and pull your shoulders back. Avoid crossing your legs or ankles and place your feet flat on the ground. Straighten the upper back.

Both sitting and standing duration should be balanced. Reducing or breaking up the sitting time with standing or walking around will enhance blood circulation, metabolism, and mental well-being.
